text:
maria: Observed a sharp increase in memory growth on kvstore during a 50k-token inference run. Paging/evictions ramped but kv_hit_rate stayed ~72%. Looks like partial residency + fragmentation causing lots of admit/evict churn. Anyone seen this pattern?

kevin: Do we have eviction counters broken down by reason and shard? eviction_total alone isn't enough. Also curious about residency percent over time.

maria: We currently export: kv_evictions_total, kv_hit_requests_total, kv_insert_bytes_total, kv_live_bytes, kv_allocated_bytes. No eviction_reason label today. Evictions spiked x3 at ~1849123000 and stayed high for the long-context run.

sahil: Can you paste a tiny profiler or some logs? Could be repeated re-materialization of KV fragments when fragments get evicted mid-sequence. That would explain the memory growth + steady hit-rate.

maria: Paste of agent logs around spike (trimmed):
```
kvstore: shard=7 evict key=ctx_abc size=128k reason=memory_pressure
kvstore: shard=7 insert key=ctx_abc size=128k
kvstore: shard=7 evict key=ctx_xyz size=64k reason=memory_pressure
kvstore: shard=7 insert key=ctx_xyz size=64k
... (repeat) ...
```
Notice the admits right after evict.

olivia: That pattern screams fragmentation + wrong LRU granularity. If we evict small fragments but later re-request them, we thrash. Two quick asks: 1) add a fragmentation ratio metric (allocated_bytes / live_bytes) per-shard, 2) add an eviction_reason label (memory_pressure|lru|ttl|rebalance).

kevin: Agreed. Also add per-key reuse counter (kv_key_reuse_total{shard,fragment_bucket}) or at least a sample-based reuse histogram. That will tell if those fragments get reaccessed right after eviction.

maria: Working on a small probe: sample 1/1000 evictions and emit a trace with the callstack + last access age. That should help correlate. Will also add a residency histogram: kv_residency_bucket with buckets for 0..100% residency.

runtime-bot: perf-bench: kv-paging-probe v1 run complete. baseline p50 latency=6.2ms, p95=12.8ms. repro run with fragmentation_ratio>0.6 -> p50=8.9ms, p95=21.4ms.

sahil: Nice. Can you post the PromQL queries we'll need for dashboards/alerts?

maria: Draft PromQLs: 
```
sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (shard, eviction_reason)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_residency_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard))
(sum(kv_live_bytes) / sum(kv_allocated_bytes)) by (shard)  # fragmentation_ratio
sum(rate(kv_key_reuse_total[5m])) by (shard)
```
These should help show where thrashing is concentrated.

kevin: For alerts: trigger when eviction rate > 3x baseline for >2m AND fragmentation_ratio > 0.5. Also alert when residency drops below 60% for a shard. We'll need runbooks.

maria: Action items: add eviction_reason label + sampled eviction traces (maria), export fragmentation_ratio + residency histogram (maria), add key_reuse sampler (maria), update dashboards (kevin), add canary long-context fuzz harness to reproduce (sahil). ETA: EOD for metrics + sampler, dashboard PR tomorrow.

olivia: One more: make sure eviction metric increments include a label for model_family so we can correlate with quantized vs fp16 models — quantization changes KV sizes and may increase fragmentation.

runtime-bot: perf-alert: created alert "kv_thrash_high" (severity=page) -> notify eng-runtime -> inspect runbook link: /runbooks/kv-thrash.

kevin: I'll draft the runbook sections (what to check: eviction_reason, fragmentation_ratio, key_reuse samples, recent deploys, model_family label).

sahil: I'll run the reproduce harness across recent kernel selection changes and a heavy-batch workload. If kernel selection changed memory layout, that could worsen fragmentation.

maria: Thanks. I'm landing a tiny PR that adds eviction_reason + fragmentation_ratio + 1/1000 eviction sampler. Pushed branch: git.redwood/kv/eviction-observability. Will ping when CI passes.

kevin: Once metrics are in, let's add a 2-panel dashboard: (1) shard heatmap: eviction_rate vs fragmentation_ratio, (2) timeline: hit_rate, residency, live_bytes.

olivia: Also add a small synthetic job that runs nightly: long-context session for 100k tokens to detect slow memory growth regressions automatically.

maria: Will add the nightly job to the perf-suite and link results in the dashboard.

kevin: Great. If anyone reproduces a regression tied to kernel selection/packing, call it out here and we can gate the rollout.

sahil: Will report back with the reproduce matrix by EOD tomorrow.

maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
